summary: Code is clean and well-documented, but one blocking issue requires a fix before approval: unbounded monkeypatch stacking on shared tool objects.

inject_project_path mutates tool.ainvoke in-place. list(mcp_tools) in nodes/__init__.py shallow-copies the list shell but not the tool objects. Every node_fn invocation therefore wraps an already-wrapped ainvoke, chaining closures indefinitely.

After N runs each tool carries N nested async wrapper frames and N live closure references — a memory leak that will degrade long-running orchestrations. Correctness is preserved (setdefault semantics flatten), but the growth is unbounded.

Fix: save the true original ainvoke once using a sentinel attribute (e.g. _orig_ainvoke) so repeated calls are idempotent. Non-blocking: add regression test in WP-005 for repeated inject_project_path calls on the same tools list.

comments.note: Unbounded wrapper stacking on shared tool objects. inject_project_path captures tool.ainvoke on each call, but list(mcp_tools) is a shallow copy — the tool objects are the same references. After the first node_fn run, tool.ainvoke is already a _wrapped_ainvoke; the second run wraps the wrapper; the Nth run has N closures chained. Fix: use a sentinel attribute to capture the true original once: `orig = getattr(tool, '_orig_ainvoke', None); if orig is None: tool._orig_ainvoke = tool.ainvoke; orig = tool._orig_ainvoke`. This makes inject_project_path idempotent.

Non-blocking: the module docstring says 'Mutation is in-place; the original list reference is also returned for convenience.' This is accurate but should note, after the sentinel fix, that subsequent calls on already-wrapped tools are idempotent.

Non-blocking (WP-005): When test_tool_wrappers.py is written, add an explicit test that calls inject_project_path twice on the same tools list and asserts ainvoke is not double-wrapped — i.e., the sentinel guard works.

comments.note: Blocking fix verified: sentinel _orig_ainvoke is stored before the first mutation. hasattr guard prevents re-wrapping on the same tool object. Default-parameter binding (_orig=_original_ainvoke, _proj=project_path) in _wrapped_ainvoke avoids late-binding issues in the loop. The wrapper chain is provably bounded to exactly one level.

Non-blocking: _wrapped_ainvoke mutates the input dict in-place via setdefault. For LangChain MCP StructuredTools, inputs are ephemeral per-call dicts so this is harmless. If LangChain ever caches or reuses input dicts, this could cause silent side-effects. A defensive copy (input = dict(input)) before setdefault would eliminate any future risk at negligible cost.
